summary.headline: Golkunda Q1 FY27 revenue rose 22.7% YoY to INR85.2 crore and EBITDA rose 69% to INR8.64 crore, with margin up to 10.14%.
summary.overview: Q1 FY27 revenue from operations was INR85.2 crore versus INR69.4 crore a year earlier, with EBITDA up about 69% to INR8.64 crore and EBITDA margin expanding from 7.35% to 10.14%. Net profit rose about 64% to INR5.14 crore (margin 6.03% vs 4.2%). Management framed the quarter as the start of a domestic diversification phase, anchored by a newly operational Andheri (Mumbai) manufacturing facility outside the SEZ. This was the company's first formal earnings call, and management said near-term volumes from the domestic facility will be small.

financial_highlights.change: +22.7% YoY vs INR69.44 crore in Q1 FY26
up from INR230 crore two years earlier
up from INR16.9 crore two years earlier (about 35%)

segments.name: Export (Middle East, USA, Europe)
segments.commentary: Middle East (UAE, Saudi Arabia, Qatar, Kuwait, Bahrain) contributes about 85-90% of total business; USA share has fallen to below 10% from 20-30% a year earlier due to tariffs. Management pegs current export run-rate at about INR280 crore.

segments.name: Domestic (Andheri, Mumbai facility)
segments.commentary: Facility covers about 5,360 sq ft with estimated capacity of 125-150 kg jewellery per annum, expected to lift overall capacity by 50-60%. Currently producing sample lines; management expects only INR15-20 crore revenue in FY27.

segments.name: Lab-grown diamond jewellery
segments.commentary: Management put lab-grown at less than 5-7% of current revenue, mainly from the US market. Domestic B2C lab-grown retail launch is targeted around Diwali (Sept-Oct 2026).

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue growth target of around 15-20%, predominantly from exports.
Domestic business targeted at about 50% of total revenue by 2030; implied revenue of INR550-600 crore on current export base.
Andheri facility peak revenue potential of around INR250-300 crore in about three years; revenue mix depends on gold carat mix (shift from 18k to 14k, 10k, 9k).
Five-year target of revenue more than double the current level.
Domestic EBITDA margin expected to be tighter initially, converging to export levels over time; B2C expected to be better margin than B2B but insignificant in FY27.
capex_capacity: Andheri, Mumbai facility (approx. 5,360 sq ft, three-storey; two storeys operational, third storey being built as a retail lounge for B2C) is up and running with 125-150 kg per annum estimated capacity.
Existing two facilities are in an SEZ and export-focused; the Andheri unit is the first outside SEZ for domestic operations.
Preferential allotment of convertible warrants (about INR27 crore) to fund facility expansion and working capital.
Inventory days cited at roughly 10-11 times for exports, with management expecting domestic to be similar or better.
demand_pricing: Retail customers are shifting from 18k to 14k, and in some cases 9k-10k gold jewellery, following gold price increases.
Top 10 customers account for approximately 60-65% of revenue (management could not give top-5 split).
Diamonds are hedged via forward contracts covering 4-6 months of receivables; gold has a natural hedge through matched import/export pricing.
Management said the Middle East revenue was not materially affected by the Hormuz disruption beyond roughly a month of air-freight stoppage from late February to March 2026.
Competition in domestic lab-grown is nascent; management named no specific head-to-head competitor and cited branded retailers and traditional jewellers as entrants.

qa_highlights.question: What is the domestic expansion strategy given competition from organised players?
qa_highlights.answer: Two-pronged: manufacture for major Indian retail chains already served in the Middle East, and pursue B2C retail, especially lab-grown, over the next two to three years.

qa_highlights.question: Is the US business exported or through a subsidiary?
qa_highlights.answer: No subsidiary; sales are to wholesalers, distributors and retailers in Middle East, USA and Europe.

qa_highlights.question: What revenue can the new capacity generate?
qa_highlights.answer: Management estimates INR250-300 crore of incremental revenue potential, subject to gold carat mix.

qa_highlights.question: What are the FY27 and 2030 targets?
qa_highlights.answer: FY27 growth of 15-20%, mainly exports; domestic to reach 50% of business by 2030, implying INR550-600 crore total on current export base.

qa_highlights.question: What are the lab-grown contribution and targets?
qa_highlights.answer: Lab-grown is under 5-7% of revenue, mostly US; management hopes it will be a significant domestic contributor but gave no numerical target.

qa_highlights.question: What is the expected FY27 revenue from the Mumbai facility and when does B2C start?
qa_highlights.answer: INR15-20 crore in FY27; B2C launch targeted around Diwali (Sept-Oct 2026), with B2C insignificant in FY27.

risks_watch: Domestic ramp is unproven: FY27 facility revenue guided at only INR15-20 crore against a 2030 target of about 50% domestic mix.
Heavy concentration: top 10 customers are about 60-65% of revenue, and Middle East is 85-90% of business.
Domestic EBITDA is expected to be thinner initially, which could dilute the 10.14% margin as B2B and B2C scale.
Gold price shifts toward lower carat jewellery and the 250-300 crore capacity estimate depend on mix assumptions.
Management said the company is still building a brand and retail experience for B2C; it gave no B2C target beyond the Diwali launch.
summary.management_tone: Confident and expansive on long-term domestic and lab-grown ambitions, but vague or deferential on specifics; several answers lacked numbers (e.g., competitors, B2C mix, margins) and the CEO had to look up top-10 customer share. Clear and specific on near-term FY27 guidance and the Middle East share.

adds.what: Andheri, Mumbai domestic jewellery facility, 125-150 kg/yr estimated capacity (~5,360 sq ft); lifts overall capacity by 50-60%

growth.why: FY27 revenue guided at 15-20% (midpoint 17.5%), Q1 grew 22.7% YoY, and the Andheri unit is up and running, though management says it adds only INR15-20 crore revenue in FY27 and the guidance is mainly export-driven.
